about: One permission fixture decided by every consumer: md's compose pre-flight and slot gate (darkmatter/lib/tests/l1/permission_parity.rs), Claudine's preparation (claudine/lib/tests/l1/shell_permission_parity.rs), and DMLS's passive classification (darkmatter/dmls/tests/l1/shell_permission_classification.rs). Each test writes `user_permissions` (plus a `network` line) to a temporary home's `.darkmatter.yaml` and `home_files` below that home. A decision is `preapproved` (runs without asking), `approval-required` (nothing approves it and nothing may ask), or `refused` (the built-in blacklist, whatever is approved). A command row with `command` is composed as `::shell <command>`, and DMLS classifies that literal; a row with `document` only is composed as written, and DMLS (which classifies literal commands only) skips it.
user_permissions:
permissions:
  file-read:
    - "~/data/*.yaml"
    - "!~/data/secret.yaml"
  shell-commands:
    - prefix echo
    - prefix chmod
    - template git --version {{ string }}
    - "!exact echo secret"

commands.name: a chain with an unlisted segment
an exclusion over a prefix allow
the built-in blacklist over a prefix allow
the built-in blacklist in one segment of an allowed chain
a template rule approves its shape
a template rule never approves a literal

file_reads.name: an exclusion over a home entry

url_reads.name: the exact host allowed for the run
another host allowed for the run
